January, 2024

Author: M.M. Sundresh
Bench: M.M. Sundresh
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No.1687/2021
 Shakuntala Bhaskar Kale & Ors. Appell
 Versus
 The State Of Maharashtra Respond
 With
 Criminal Appeal No.2365/2023
 O R D E R
1.
Heard learned Senior Counsel for the parties.

2. Criminal Appeal No.1687/2021 has been filed by accused Nos.2 to 4 while Criminal Appeal No.2365/2023 is filed by accused No.1.
3.
The case of the prosecution in nutshell is that the deceased was married to accused no.1 on 08.03.2010.
The second accused is the father-in-law, third accused is the mother-in-law and the fourth one is the sister-in-law of the deceased.
It is the case of the prosecution that the deceased was subjected to continuous mental and physical cruelty at the hands of all the accused.
In fact, she was threatened by pouring kerosene on her by accused Nos.1 and 4 at an earlier occasion.
p.m. within two years of the marriage.
The first informant being the brother of the deceased along with his parents rushed to the home of the accused in which the deceased was living and found her lying dead with injuries on her neck.
Ironically, the accused were not present in the house.
The postmortem report done also indicated that the death occurred due to strangulation and ante-mortem injuries were also found on the body of the deceased.
Though there was a bottle of poison found near the deceased, the test indicated that she has not consumed it.
5. During questioning, all the accused denied the charges levied.

In support of the prosecution version, nine witnesses have been examined including PW1 who is the complainant brother of the deceased and PW2 and PW6 being the mother and another brother of the deceased.
PW4 is the grandfather of the deceased.

sentences.text: On behalf of the appellants, three witnesses have been examined.

7. The Trial Court upon finding that an offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC being made out applied the presumption under Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 and found that the appellant in Criminal Appeal No.2365/2023 is liable to be punished for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304B IPC.
Insofar as Criminal Appeal No.1687/2021 is concerned

, the Trial Court despite a similar finding being rendered against accused no.1 and without giving any specific finding for not attracting Section 304B of the IPC, against the appellants acquitted them for the said charge while convicting them under Section 498A of the IPC.
Both the appellants and the prosecution filed appeals.

By the impugned order the High Court of Bombay Judicature at Aurangabad, while confirming the conviction and sentence rendered by the Trial Court insofar as A1 is concerned, allowed the appeal filed by the State, by convicting A2- A4 qua the offence under Section 304B of the IPC.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 8. Aggrieved, both the appeals are before us.

9. The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that the Trial Court, having noted the demeanor of the witnesses extended the benefit of doubt in favour of the appellants in Criminal Appeal No.1687/2021 and therefore, the presumption having been strengthened, the High Court ought not replace it with its views.
Insofar as A1 is concerned, it is submitted that there is no clear evidence to implicate him though at the time of occurrence, the deceased was living with him.

The evidence of the doctor coupled with the postmortem report cannot be the sole basis to implicate him.
10.
The learned counsel appearing for the State took us to the reasoning rendered by both the courts below.

It is submitted by learned Senior Counsel that strangely, the Court of Sessions despite rendering all the findings against the accused in Criminal Appeal No.1687/2021, acquitted them without assigning any specific reasons.

On the contrary, the High Court under the impugned order,
rightly considered the evidence available on record including that of DW1 to DW3.
Therefore, no interference is required.
11. We have perused the materials available on record including the evidence adduced by the witnesses.

In our considered view, both the courts have rightly held that the appellants are guilty of the offences committed, though the Trial Court, without any reasons having been assigned,
acquitted the appellants in criminal Appeal No.1687/2021, qua the charge framed under Section 304B IPC.
Admittedly, the death occurred at the home of the appellants.

Though the learned Senior Counsel contended that there is no clear evidence to show that all the appellants were residing in the same place, both the courts have disbelieved the evidence adduced on behalf of the appellants through DW1 to DW3.
The relationship between the parties is not in dispute.
Incidentally, the place of occurrence belongs to A4.
In such view of the matter, there is no perversity in the finding rendered by the courts below for attracting the offence punishable under Section 498A of the IPC.

By taking note of the evidence available on record coupled with the conduct of the appellants by placing reliance upon Section 8 of the Indian Evidence Act, that they were not present after the occurrence which was only noted by PW1, we are inclined to confirm the conviction rendered under Shakuntala Bhaskar Kale vs The State Of Maharashtra on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89100450/
2 the impugned order.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. At this juncture, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellants submitted that the appellant nos.2 and 3 in Criminal Appeal No.1687 of 2021 are women and the first appellant is an aged person.
The Trial Court also acquitted them for the charge under Section 304B of the IPC.

Insofar as the appellant in Criminal Appeal No.2365/2023 is concerned, he has already undergone about 13 years of incarceration with remission and, therefore, the sentence will not be reduced.
13.
The learned counsel appearing for the State submitted that there is no need to interfere with the sentence awarded by the High Court.
14. The offence took place on 04.03.2012.
Nearly 12 years have lapsed since then.
Out of the four accused, two ladies are mother and daughter (widow), A2 is an aged man.
A1 has already undergone 13 years of incarceration.
There is no clear evidence available as to who committed the offence and that is why both the courts have acquitted of charge under Section 304B of the IPC.

15. Taking into consideration these mitigating factors, we are inclined to modify the sentence awarded against the appellants while confirming conviction.
16.

Accordingly, the sentence of the appellant in Criminal Appeal No.2365 of 2023 is modified to the one undergone already while that of appellants in Criminal Appeal No.1687 of 2021 stands modified to 7 years of rigorous imprisonment.
17. The appeals are allowed in part.
18. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
